logline: A commitment-phobic plastic surgeon hires a cheerfully marriage-obsessed woman as his fake girlfriend to repel his parents' matchmaking - then watches the arrangement spin completely out of control.

bollymeter.basis: MyDramaList users rate it 8.0/10 across nearly 29,000 votes; IMDb overall score sits at 7.5/10. Audience consensus points to one of the cleanest execution of the fake-dating premise in the genre, anchored by Han Groo and Yeon Woo-jin's precise comic timing.

seasons.review_body: Marriage, Not Dating aired on tvN in summer 2014, averaging 1.97 percent viewership on cable with episode 13 peaking at 3.31 percent - respectable numbers for a cable romcom in that era. The drama's international reputation has grown considerably since, with MyDramaList users (nearly 29,000 ratings) consistently placing it among the strongest examples of the fake-dating genre. What audience reviews cluster on is restraint: the show avoids the extended misunderstanding arcs that derail most K-drama romcoms, letting the genuine chemistry between Gong Gi-tae and Joo Jang-mi evolve with unusual honesty. Yeon Woo-jin plays the anti-marriage surgeon with dry wit that stops short of unlikability, and Han Groo's Jang-mi is refreshingly active rather than reactive. The secondary love lines are thinner, and the villain motivation is formulaic, but the central pairing earns its conclusion.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The fake-girlfriend contract is established with brisk comic economy - the show wastes no time getting both leads into the same orbit and immediately mining the situational absurdity.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Gi-tae's horrified expression when Jang-mi enthusiastically charms his entire family at first meeting.

episode_reviews.title: Nevertheless, Marriage
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale (rated 8.1 on IMDb per episode page) pays off the central irony with satisfying completeness - a man who engineered a fake relationship learning what a real one requires.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final wedding sequence that reframes everything the season built toward.
